#3129. The Trade Desk Stock is Suddenly on Fire. Here’s Why.

The digital advertising pioneer may have finally turned the corner. Only time will tell.

There's no sugarcoating it: The Trade Desk (TTD +15.47%) has lost much of its luster over the past 18 months. When the company reported its Q4 results in early 2025, investors were taken aback. The Trade Desk had fallen short of its own forecast, marking the first time in 33 consecutive quarters the company missed the mark. It's been largely downhill ever since. The stock had lost 90% of its value, plagued by decelerating revenue growth and falling profits. Despite management's best efforts to right the ship, there was little in the way of good news. Until today, that is.

Anticipation ahead of The Trade Desk's financial report and word that one of the company's co-founders was rejoining the fold sparked a rebound, and the release of The Trade Desk's results further fanned the flames. Investors let out a collective cheer.

The Trade Desk's third-quarter results went a long way toward assuring investors that the company has turned a corner. Revenue declined 0.5% to $736 million. The bottom line held up better than expected, though adjusted EBITDA declined 16% to $266 million, driving adjusted earnings per share (EPS) down nearly 27% to $0.33.

While that might not seem like a reason to celebrate, consider this: Management's outlook was for revenue of $650 million and adjusted EBITDA of $160 million, so the results cleared both hurdles with ease.

Even Wall Street was caught off guard, as analysts' consensus estimates were calling for revenue of $651.4 million and adjusted EPS of $0.25, so The Trade Desk sailed past expectations with room to spare.

The Trade Desk also maintained its history of strong customer retention, which remained above 95% during the quarter, a track record that goes back more than a decade.

CEO Jeff Green noted that "Q3 represented meaningful progress with results well ahead of our expectations entering the quarter." He went on to say that, while there's still more work to do, the company is "moving with greater urgency" to right the ship.

The better-than-expected results come on the heels of another important announcement. Last week, The Trade Desk announced the return of co-founder and former chief technology officer (CTO) Dave Pickles, who stepped down in 2023.

Pickles and Green co-founded The Trade Desk in 2009 after working together at the digital ad exchange AdECN, where Pickles and his team built the entire ad exchange in less than seven months. The company was ultimately acquired by Microsoft in 2007.

As the creator and architect of The Trade Desk's adtech system, Pickles knows the platform better than anyone, according to Green. That deep knowledge and expertise help explain why the stock jumped more than 15% on Monday, giving investors hope that his skills will help facilitate The Trade Desk's recovery.

Beyond the quarter's financial results, investors were pleased with The Trade Desk's vision for the future. For the upcoming fourth quarter, management's outlook called for revenue of at least $755 million and adjusted EBITDA of $280 million. While that will mark sequential gains, it would still represent year-over-year declines of 11% and 30%, respectively.

For context, analysts' consensus estimates called for Q4 revenue of $691 million, so The Trade Desk's guidance was still significantly ahead of Wall Street's predictions.

As a longtime shareholder, I'm cautiously optimistic. While I'm glad to see The Trade Desk making meaningful progress, the real test will be whether the company can maintain its upward trajectory. I personally will want to see another quarter or two of results headed in the right direction before I cue up the victory march.

Even after Monday's rally, The Trade Desk stock is selling for just 15 times earnings. While that's an intriguing valuation, I think the company still has more to prove before I would add any shares.

Danny Vena, CPA has positions in Microsoft and The Trade Desk. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Microsoft and The Trade Desk. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy.

#3128. As AI becomes more fractured, one name stands out: AMD

As Anthropic rushes to takes its shares public, the AI trade is showing cracks, and they are not confined to fringe players.

We recently wrote about CoreWeave, which fell 15.5% on Oct. 14 as yields on its 2032 notes touched 15%, and its default-swap spreads nearly doubled in October. IREN is down more than 20% this year. Last Thursday, the contagion reached chipmakers, which makes sense since much of CRWV and IREN's spending is going there. AMD dropped 8.1% as Meta's financing plans and a supply warning from Lam Research exacerbated data-center fears about the pace of AI spending.

Because when you screen for factors that demonstrably generate outperformance over time, the list narrows quickly. My screen: price above the 200-day moving average; revenue growing at least as fast as the S&P 500 (5%+ per annum); EPS growing at least as fast (7%+); rating upgrades; a PEG below 3; and ROE and ROIC of at least 12%. Of the names reporting in the next two weeks, AMD is effectively the only one that makes the list. Yes, you can (and arguably should, as our staples article described) position your portfolio with slightly less tech exposure than the broad indices provide, but we can't ignore the market's biggest and most transformative sector entirely.

Especially because the growth in this case doesn't just meet my criteria; it blows past them. Consensus for Q3 calls for EPS of $1.94 on revenue of $13.06 billion, versus $1.20 and $9.25 billion a year ago. That's YoY growth of nearly 62% and 41%, respectively. The recent drawdown came from a sector selloff, not anything AMD reported, but it shows that if some names in the space get hit, even the larger players are likely to feel it. On Oct. 6, Lisa Su said AMD would substantially increase supply in 2027 because AI orders keep outrunning capacity.

So how do you balance factors we know work for a fast-growing company against a backdrop of cracks in the AI trade? Options.

Owning the stock outright means absorbing a roughly 9% to 11% implied earnings-related move (day of). Earnings are about a week out, and over the past four quarters the smallest move over a similar window was more than 9%, and the largest move, after the company reported its Q1 26 results, was 38%! Of course, that kind of volatility means options aren't cheap, and that rich premium is also a reason not to simply buy calls.

A call spread risk reversal does both jobs: it reduces risk if the cracks widen, and the short options offset the elevated volatility we would otherwise pay for. The bottom chart shows that, by sacrificing about $1,700 of upside for $5,000 in outperformance during a severe downside move, and given how jittery this trade has been lately, this is a way to stay in it with considerably less risk. $5,000 less, specifically. Of course, selling that out will tie up some cash, but less so than simply buying the stock. And selling both the out and the call reduces long call purchase by 66%

#3125. How to Use AI Tools Like ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude to Prep for a Job Interview

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

AI makes it easy to rehearse a job interview as many times as you need, with feedback after every answer.

ChatGPT’s voice mode lets you run a spoken mock interview and hear follow-up questions in real time.

For job seekers, the job interview can feel like an endurance test of their skills and personality.

It’s enough to make a person yearn for the simpler days of newspaper ads and in-person handshakes. But alas, we find ourselves immersed in the era of smart homes and Bluetooth-enabled blueberry mint vapes. But AI offers one practical advantage: a way to rehearse before the real thing.

A chatbot can play the role of a hiring manager, ask questions likely to come up for a specific job and tell you — bluntly, if you want — where your answers fall flat. That makes AI chatbots some of the more practical interview prep tools available, especially since you can rehearse as many times as you need without leaning on a friend’s patience. These chatbots can also help you research the company, prepare stories that answer common behavioral questions and get a rough sense of what the role should pay.

Here are a couple of ways you can leverage AI tools to ace your next job interview.

Read more: The New Age of Hiring: AI Is Changing the Game for Job Seekers

How you look in a job interview matters. Even if you’re sitting at home pantsless and just woke up from a nap, you gotta look the part on Zoom.

You can ask ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude to generate Zoom backgrounds that showcase your understanding of and affinity for the company culture.

Gemini created these backgrounds for my theoretical job interviews with Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, Apple, Google, Netflix and more.

Some of them turned out a little better than others, but you get the idea.

Some states, like California, have made it all but mandatory for employers to post the salary range for jobs they post as vacant. Even if you might know the salary range of the job going into the interview, the topic of compensation is always best approached with as much information as possible.

I asked Google’s Gemini AI to reference Glassdoor listings, public earnings, expenditure announcements, shareholder communications, and online media results for the salary ranges of the CEOs at Meta, Amazon, Apple, Microsoft, Netflix, and Alphabet and to provide me with salary ranges for mid-level marketing professionals at those companies.

Gemini then gave me a five-year growth schedule, where it laid out how I could begin to make more money by leveraging my sign-on bonus in the first year, my vesting stock in the second, a raise in the third, a title change in the fourth and a big promotion in the fifth (very idealistic, but it could happen).

Gemini also provided more information on how each of those companies typically structures your compensation — whether it’s an all-cash salary, one with built-in bonuses, or employee stock options. It’s important to have this information when you’re asked about the salary you expect.

Most guides on how to land a gig suggest that job seekers research the company, its culture and what the role entails. But honestly, job seekers are already investing a tremendous amount of time applying to open positions and going through multiple rounds of interviews.

What’s more important is your ability to effectively explain why you’re perfect for the job.

For my hypothetical marketing role, I used Claude to research the CMOs at those companies, including their social posts and their teams’ major priorities. I asked the AI tool to give me some one-word anchors for interview talking points, cross-referenced to elements of my resume that would be directly applicable.

It gave me some keywords to bring up, and how to relate them back to my own resume, listed out CEOs’ vision and products, told me which company could be my biggest opportunity and best fit and why — and how to express that in an interview:

Nerves are normal in a high-stakes communication like a job interview. You’re trying to appear interested but not desperate, competent but not cocky, and decide on a salary requirement you won’t live to regret.

One way to get your mind right for the job interview and take the edge off could be using an AI tool to run through some sample interview questions with you.

Several online platforms offer features that let you run a trial before your interview, including Final Round AI, which offers real-time interview transcription and support, mock interviews and resume building. Another platform, Yoodli, focuses on AI-powered communication coaching to improve both verbal and nonverbal delivery and offers AI roleplays. You can also talk with Gemini Live and get real-time responses.

In my case, I asked ChatGPT via the voice chat feature to pretend it was the hiring manager for a job at a fictitious company that sells subscription dog-sitting services, and to act as if it was unimpressed by my resume to give me a challenge and desensitize me to the worst-case scenario.

While the text chat was more of a critique of my resume, bless its sweet little machine algorithm, ChatGPT in voice chat was way too nice to even get into character for this challenge, no matter how I prompted it.

AI tools can be effective options for job seekers who don’t feel comfortable reaching out to someone in their network to help them prepare. Always keep in mind, however, that AI tools come with pitfalls, including issues related to data collection, bias and inconsistent messaging.

Use AI to prepare, but don’t let it fake your performance. AI doesn’t replace genuine networking, and the guiding principle should be to stay authentic.

#3123. Samsung’s new SmartTag 3 debuts with next-gen Bluetooth – and one big problem

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

The Galaxy SmartTag 3 supports emerging Bluetooth tracking tech, but it's not a match for Samsung's OS exclusivity.

Samsung’s Galaxy SmartTag 3 is now available for purchase in the US, promising a smaller, lighter design than previous generations, compatibility with iOS devices, 550 days of battery life, an NFC-powered Lost Mode, Left Behind Alerts, and an IP67 dust- and water-resistant rating.

Though the Galaxy SmartTag 3 is compatible with iOS devices, the features available to Apple fans are limited, with Ring Phone, Left Behind Alerts, and Compass View reserved for Galaxy users. Compass View is enabled by Bluetooth Channel Sounding, an upgraded Bluetooth distance-finding technology. Despite Samsung embracing a low-cost boost to device tracking, Channel Sounding is locked inside the Galaxy ecosystem, a blow to the technology’s intended purpose.

Also: 3 ways Bluetooth 7 upgrades your devices beyond lossless audio

Channel Sounding is also Google’s Pixel Tag and Motorola’s Moto Tag 2, but these manufacturers open the technology to all compatible Android phones. However, Samsung’s SmartTag 3 doesn’t rely on Android’s vast but fragmented Find My Device network; instead, Samsung’s take on Channel Sounding will rely exclusively on the Galaxy Find Network. If a semi-closed ecosystem can help make evolving Bluetooth tech more reliable, does it matter that its implementation is counterproductive?

Samsung is the Goldilocks of device ecosystems. It’s not considered a walled garden like Apple, but it’s not as open to full third-party interoperability as Google. Many of Samsung’s most useful features are reserved for use within its Galaxy ecosystem. However, Samsung’s OS is built on top of Android, allowing for more flexibility than iOS, but still offering OS-exclusive features and, more importantly, feature reliability.

Full access to Samsung’s Galaxy Find Network is exclusive to Galaxy devices, similar to how full access to Apple’s Find My tracking features is reserved for Apple devices. On the other hand, Google’s Find Hub can accommodate Android phones from several manufacturers, including Samsung.

Also: Android is getting my favorite iOS tracking feature – what to expect

According to a press release, nearly 900 million Galaxy devices exist on the Galaxy Find Network. Each one’s constant Bluetooth signals contribute to an expansive network of crowdsourced data, extending the Galaxy FindTag 3’s reach and surfacing location data faster.

Google’s Find Hub’s greatest benefit is its scale: it can work with headphones, earbuds, Bluetooth trackers, smartphones, and smartwatches from multiple manufacturers.

However, different ecosystems limit tracking features to basic functionality, showing only where a device was last seen before it was powered off, or emitting a chime if you lose it. Live location data and accurate direction and distance finding from your smartphone aren’t possible.

Also: Apple has a Bluetooth problem, and Android is taking advantage

Implementing Bluetooth Channel Sounding aims to break down ecosystem-specific barriers, especially in a device-tracking context. If your smartphone, headphones, and smartwatch all support Channel Sounding, you could access fine-ranging tracking on all of them, regardless of device manufacturer.

Despite Samsung’s ecosystem providing it a device-tracking advantage, it defeats the purpose of Bluetooth: democratization. Basic Bluetooth connectivity allows any Bluetooth-compatible device to connect to another; that’s why you can wirelessly pair a pair of AirPods with a Lenovo laptop.

Also: Google’s Pixel Tag tracker has a big advantage over AirTags

Channel Sounding’s goal is no different in that it aims to bring more accurate distance awareness to Bluetooth-enabled devices, allowing you to finely track a pair of Sony headphones with an iPhone — that’s the goal, but not yet reality.

Samsung instead adopted Channel Sounding for its first consumer-ready endpoint within the boundaries of its ecosystem. Only Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, Galaxy Z Fold 8, Galaxy S26 Ultra, and Galaxy S26 Plus users can unlock the Galaxy SmartTag 3’s Channel Sounding capabilities when engaging its Compass View feature.

Also: Beware of Bluetooth sniffers: How your favorite gadgets could be exposing your data

All of these phones support Bluetooth 6.0 and Channel Sounding, but the Galaxy SmartTag 3’s Channel Sounding abilities will only be available to them and future Galaxy phones with Channel Sounding.

Conversely, Google’s Pixel Tag offers Channel Sounding to all Android phones that support it, including Galaxy phones. The result is that the Galaxy SmartTag 3 will operate just like any other Bluetooth tracker when paired with a base-model flagship phone, an older Galaxy phone, or an iPhone.

During this year’s WWDC, Apple announced Channel Sounding support for iPhones with its N1 networking chip and third-party Bluetooth 6.3 devices. Bluetooth 6.3 devices aren’t on the market yet and won’t be for a few years.

I assume Apple’s announcement of faraway future support is to give itself time to decide how Channel Sounding will fit into its walled garden, similar to Samsung’s implementation in the Galaxy SmartTag 3.

Also: How to tell if a hidden AirTag is tracking you – and disable it ASAP

Sure, Google’s Find Hub still needs some maturing; just last year, Google boosted the opt-in opportunities to add more devices for crowdsourced data, Find People is coming to Wear OS, and Find Hub is getting “Notify when left behind” alerts soon.

Apple’s and Samsung’s device location networks may be more feature-rich thanks to their closed ecosystems, but Google is working toward a truly open, easy-to-use network of devices powered by Channel Sounding. Which one is more important to you is for you to decide when it’s time to make a purchase.

#3122. NASA’s Voyager 1 to Cross Historic One Light-Day Milestone on Nov. 18

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Traveling one light-day took the space probe 49 years. it would take a human 612,015 years to walk that distance.

NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft is on track to set another historic record as its mission approaches the half-century mark. On Nov. 18 at 5:16 a.m. ET, the probe will reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, a journey of nearly five decades that places it farther from our planet than any human-made object in history.

It’s quite an accomplishment for a spacecraft built in the mid-1970s One light-day is the distance that light travels in a single day at the speed of light, which is approximately 186,282 miles per second. That translates to 25.9 billion kilometers or about 16.1 billion miles in a single day. At an average human walking speed of 3 mph, it would take a human 612,015 years to walk that distance.

Fortunately, Voyager 1 has been traveling a bit faster than that. It currently zips along the cosmos at a steady 37,763 mph, a speed it achieved in 1980 after a gravity-assisted Saturn flyby. It has been flying at that speed ever since.

The milestone comes 14 years after its previous one, when Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause, the point where the sun’s heliosphere ends, and entered interstellar space. It’s also 28 years after passing Pioneer 10 to become the human-made object that has traveled the farthest into space.

The historic milestone isn’t without its drama. Voyager 1 has been in space for nearly half a century, and in that time, NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory has done everything it can to extend the life of Voyager 1. That includes troubleshooting issues, performing maintenance and shutting down various systems to save power and extend the spacecraft’s life-span.

Several of those efforts took place in 2026. The team running Voyager 1 spent weeks shutting down three devices and powering on three low-power alternatives to reduce overall power usage. This initiative, which was internally called The Big Bang, was also performed on Voyager 2. The transition was completed in early September, giving Voyager 1 more time with its dwindling power supply while also keeping it warm enough to continue operating in the frigid conditions of interstellar space.

It was a tricky maneuver that required the team to simultaneously turn multiple instruments on and off. The difficulty of the maneuver was amplified by the fact that it took almost a full day for any signal to reach Voyager and another full day for Voyager to send a signal back, with hours of downtime while the spacecraft performed the operations.

All of this took place several months after Voyager 1 experienced a sudden drop in power, which necessitated shutting off one of its three remaining instruments still in operation. Voyager 1 now has only two instruments still in operation.

Making it a whole light-day away from Earth is likely going to be Voyager 1’s final milestone while it still has enough power to communicate with Earth. Voyager 1 is powered by three radioisotope thermoelectric generators. They are essentially nuclear-powered batteries that generate energy by converting the steady heat from decaying plutonium-238.

When Voyager 1 first launched, its radioisotope thermoelectric generators produced about 470 watts of power. But plutonium-238 doesn’t last forever, and after 50 years in space, the RTGs now produce about 215 watts of power, with an average loss of about 4 watts per year. Most of that power is used to keep Voyager 1 up and running, which is why NASA has shut down eight of the 10 instruments that Voyager had when it launched.

At its current rate of usage and decay, Voyager 1 is expected to shut down its final science instrument in the 2030s and will eventually lose communication with Earth in 2036 due to insufficient power to send back a radio signal.

The same fate is expected for Voyager 2, Voyager 1’s twin, which has also spent half a century in space. While it is labeled the sequel, Voyager 2 actually launched 16 days before Voyager 1, and the two have spent nearly identical amounts of time traversing the cosmos. Thanks to its slower speed and trajectory, it likely won’t reach the one light-day distance until after its instruments shut down.

Thanks to the vastness of space, Voyager 1 will lose all of its power before it hits its next milestone, which is the beginning of the Oort Cloud, a vast, icy shell of comets at the edge of our solar system. It’ll take about 300 years for Voyager 1 to make it there.

Thanks to the near-perfect vacuum of outer space, Voyager 1 will continue to fly at its current speed even after it shuts down entirely. So it’ll still hit that milestone; it just won’t be able to phone home to tell us about it.

Ionis's $1.9 billion cash pile buys time, but it is still to be seen whether patient switches to DAWNZERA can offset a slower TRYNGOLZA launch.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 9, 2026, Ionis (IONS -21.36%) lowered its full-year TRYNGOLZA revenue guidance to approximately $50 million. Commercial execution across new product launches dictates how quickly the business turns its research investments into long-term profits. Three things management said stand out.

TRYNGOLZA treats severe hypertriglyceridemia, a condition marked by elevated blood fat levels that raise acute pancreatitis risks. Doctors must adopt a new treatment approach for patients, which lengthens the time needed to build prescription volumes.

DAWNZERA treats hereditary angioedema, a rare genetic disorder that causes severe swelling attacks. Repeat prescribing and patient switches from existing preventive options expanded product revenue throughout the period.

Product expansion and mid-stage clinical trials drive the next phase. Patient switches to DAWNZERA, an expanding commercial team, and established partnerships provide structural durability while management monitors prescriber conversion.

Execution across research programs and commercial launches remains central to long-term value creation.

#3116. Ripple strikes deal with Robinhood to expand its RLUSD digital dollar

Ripple has struck a deal with Robinhood to expand the reach of its digital dollar, RLUSD, strengthening trading and financing links between their institutional businesses and improving Robinhood's internal money management.

The partnership involves using RLUSD to settle institutional trades, automate Robinhood's treasury operations and expand access to digital asset trading and financing through Ripple Prime and Bitstamp, the global crypto exchange acquired by Robinhood last year.

It also helps meet Robinhood's ambition of becoming a global financial superapp, centralizing its customers' financial lives while expanding the underlying infrastructure that can serve both retail and institutional clients.

"Utility is what moves stablecoins forward. Working with Ripple, Bitstamp and Robinhood will have access to RLUSD for institutional settlement, Ripple Treasury for our operations and Ripple Prime for financing," Robinhood Crypto General Manager Johann Kerbrat said in a statement shared with CNBC. "That is what a connected, global financial system looks like."

Stablecoins have long been a workhorse of the crypto world, giving traders a way to move money among exchanges, buy and sell crypto assets, and park funds between trades without having to convert back into traditional currency. But as the crypto industry evolves beyond trading and markets move toward 24/7 liquidity, stablecoins are becoming essential financial infrastructure because of their ability to enable near-instant settlement and move dollar-denominated value at any time, regardless of traditional banking hours.

As firms look to do more with stablecoins beyond simply listing them on exchanges, stablecoin issuers are betting they'll favor a one-stop-shop approach that bundles the technology and services needed to move money, settle trades and manage cash.

"Stablecoins have evolved from a crypto trading tool into a critical piece of financial infrastructure," Ripple President Monica Long told CNBC. "The clearest evidence of this is where they're now being embedded — from corporate payments to capital markets. Our partnership with Robinhood reflects that evolution."

"This is about much more than trading," she added. "It's about fundamentally changing how money moves and is managed — giving institutions the ability to operate 24/7/365, unlocking liquidity and putting capital to work more efficiently."

Circle Internet Group, a Ripple competitor, is positioning itself for a similar future, where winning platforms, in addition to issuing stablecoins, also provide the infrastructure to put them to work. Earlier this year, for example, it launched the Circle Payments Network, connecting financial institutions and payment providers using its flagship USDC stablecoin and other digital assets for cross-border payments.

The network is Circle's answer to the 8-year-old Ripple Payments business, a service that helps businesses move money across borders, using any of several assets moving through that system, including USDC, Ripple-created XRP and, as of its debut in December 2024, RLUSD.

RLUSD's market cap has grown to more than $2.5 billion. Tether's USDT and Circle's USDC still dominate the total stablecoin market, which now exceeds $300 billion.

RLUSD will also be listed on Robinhood's trading platform, and is currently available to traders on Bitstamp as well as Robinhood Chain, the company's home-grown blockchain for tokenized stocks and other assets.

Robinhood, which reports third-quarter results for the three months ended in September after the market closes, rose about 2.5% in early trading Tuesday, snapping a three-day decline.

Correction: A previous headline misspelled RLUSD.

Apple's public-facing satisfaction with the Siri AI launch obscures internal pressures and tensions.

Apple’s recently appointed CEO, John Ternus, is allegedly pushing the company internally to ramp up its AI strategy — including making Siri an AI agent.

Also: My 5 favorite Siri AI ‘onscreen awareness’ tricks

According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the CEO is publicly pleased with the Siri AI launch, but privately encouraging Craig Federighi, Apple’s SVP of software engineering, to move faster.

“Desiring more and frustrated by what he sees as a reluctance to embrace AI with the same urgency as competitors, Ternus pushed his software chief to accelerate the company’s road map and move quickly beyond merely making necessary improvements to Siri,” Gurman wrote. He added that the tension stems from Federighi’s reputation as an AI skeptic.

The revamped Siri AI is now a much better voice assistant with some helpful features. Gurman noted he thinks Siri AI’s ability to automatically fix your weak passwords is already somewhat agentic behavior, though AI-generated passwords have their own issues.

But Siri AI isn’t yet on par with increasingly autonomous agents from AI-first companies that aim to proactively organize your tasks, use your computer, and write advanced code. Still, those rival agents deliver a patchwork of capabilities: while some, like OpenClaw and Anthropic’s Claude Code, are highly functional, others, like Google’s Gemini Spark, aren’t quite there yet.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a free local AI stack

Regardless, the issue here is time. Despite developing powerful hardware perfectly suited for running local AI models, Apple has remained slower than competitors on the AI software front. Competitors have demonstrated they can make promised agent features a reality, some quicker than others.

On the other hand, the fact that Apple hyped Siri AI for two years only to release an improved voice assistant (rather than a groundbreaking AI product) may mean users are ready for more advanced features.

In addition, AI companies are working on their own hardware. “If they can combine that software with AI-native devices designed from the ground up around assistants that see, remember and act, Apple’s longstanding advantages could begin to matter less,” Gurman wrote.

An agentic Siri would most likely build on what users already like about the new version.

The on-screen awareness feature, for example, is currently limited to what’s visible on your screen in that moment, meaning only the part of a long email that you’ve actively scrolled to. An agentic Siri could ideally scroll all the way through an email on its own and surface the insights you’re looking for.

Also: The iPhone made Apple a giant – but the Mac could help it win the AI era

But in the short term, Ternus’ push will likely just deliver on existing promises. Gurman also pointed out that Siri AI still lacks advanced in-app actions, which Apple initially announced in 2024 and would let third-party apps create plug-ins for and pathways through Siri.

“This functionality would let Siri tap into both in-house and third-party applications with more precision,” Gurman wrote. “This past week, as part of the first beta version of iOS 27.3, Apple finally began talking about the feature again.”

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, ZDNET’s parent company, filed an April 2025 lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

Plus, if we’re talking about agents specifically, newcomers like OpenAI’s Dot and Anthropic’s Duet aren’t competitive themselves yet: ZDNET’s AI vetter-in-residence David Gewirtz found both to be “a little odd” and not “quite ready for prime time”.

Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks – and all I got was one helpful notification

For users who appreciate the subtlety of Siri AI, though, anything similar to ChatGPT or Claude on their devices might not land, unless each feature is opt-in.

Finally, our Chief Financial Officer, Bob DeLucia, will recap Sharplink's third quarter financial results, liquidity position and key ETH treasury performance metrics. So with that, I would now like to turn the call over to Sharplink's Chairman, Joe Lubin. Joe, the floor is yours.

Joseph Lubin: Thank you, Dodi, and good morning, everyone. Ethereum continues to evolve from a pioneering blockchain network into foundational infrastructure for an increasingly programmable global financial system. Its combination of security, credible neutrality, composability and next-generation trust infrastructure via rigorous decentralization provides shared financial infrastructure that institutions can build upon without relying on commercial intermediaries. Stablecoins, tokenized real-world assets and decentralized financial applications are increasingly operating on Ethereum, strengthening its already dominant network effects and expanding its role in the global economy. The scale of Ethereum's existing financial ecosystem, including Layer 2 networks, demonstrates its leadership.

Approximately $153 billion in stablecoin supply is supported by the broader Ethereum ecosystem, approximately $17 billion in tokenized real-world asset active AUM, representing approximately 55% of the tracked market, more than $58 billion in DeFi total value locked, representing approximately 65% of the global DeFi TVL, and approximately 1.8 million transactions per day on Ethereum mainnet, not counting the large amount of additional activity across its Layer 2 ecosystem. We believe Ethereum's 11-year track record of security, credible neutrality and reliable execution has established a foundation of trust that is particularly important for institutional adoption. Unlike proprietary financial networks controlled by individual intermediaries, Ethereum provides neutral infrastructure that competitive institutions can build upon with confidence.

Combined with its deep liquidity and extensive developer ecosystem, these characteristics reinforce Ethereum's position as foundational infrastructure for the next generation of global finance. One of the most significant developments during Q3 and subsequent to quarter end has been the continued acceleration of institutional adoption with some of the world's largest financial institutions deploying live financial applications directly on Ethereum. JPMorgan expanded JPM Coin, JPMD, its institutional deposit token, to Ethereum mainnet on October 19, complementing its existing deployment on the Base network. The bank specifically cited Ethereum's deep on-chain liquidity and established tokenized asset ecosystem as key reasons for the expansion, demonstrating how major financial institutions are moving beyond experimentation and increasingly utilizing Ethereum to support real-world financial activity.

Morgan Stanley expanded access to ETH through the July launch of its Ethereum Trust, MSSE, an exchange-traded investment product incorporating Ethereum staking as well as the rollout of direct currency trading on E*TRADE. Revolut, which serves more than 75 million customers globally, introduced phased testing of its euro-backed EURR stablecoin on Ethereum in August, demonstrating Ethereum's expanding role in programmable money and digital payments. ARK Invest announced the tokenization of its approximately $1.3 billion ARK Venture Fund on Ethereum in September, bringing a traditional investment strategy involving private and public growth companies onto blockchain infrastructure. Institutional adoption is also accelerating across other major financial platforms.

In August, BlackRock expanded its tokenization initiatives with the launch of Ethereum-based share classes for select European UCITS money market funds alongside 2 new U.S. tokenized money market products, BSTBL and BRSRV. Credit Agricole also introduced EURXT, a euro-denominated stablecoin issued on Ethereum. These developments demonstrate Ethereum's expanding role across institutional asset management, payments and financial market infrastructure with major financial institutions increasingly choosing Ethereum to support real-world financial applications. As more institutions bring assets, liquidity and financial activity on chain, we believe Ethereum's network effects will continue strengthening, reinforcing its position as foundational infrastructure for the next generation of global finance.

Alongside accelerating institutional adoption, Ethereum continues to advance its protocol road map to support significantly greater transaction volumes, improve efficiency and strengthen long-term resilience. Following the successful implementation of previous network upgrades, Ethereum continues to advance towards Glamsterdam, its next major protocol update. Glamsterdam is designed to improve Ethereum's ability to process more transactions in parallel and therefore, more efficiently while reducing reliance on trusted third parties outside the protocol that emerged to support the separation of the block proposer and block builder roles. These improvements reinforce one of Ethereum's greatest competitive advantages, its commitment to credible neutrality, decentralization and censorship resistance at scale.

Together, these initiatives reflect Ethereum's commitment to becoming the foundational infrastructure for global finance, delivering greater speed, capacity and efficiency without compromising the security, credible neutrality and decentralization that distinguish the network. We believe Ethereum's continued ability to evolve technologically while maintaining its core principles will be an important differentiator as institutional adoption accelerates. Ethereum's expanding institutional adoption and ongoing technological advancements strengthen our conviction in its long-term role as foundational infrastructure for the global digital economy. As financial activity increasingly moves on chain, ETH remains integral to securing the network, facilitating transactions and supporting the broader ecosystem of programmable financial applications.

Sharplink is strategically positioned to participate in Ethereum's next phase of growth through its actively managed ETH treasury, institutional expertise and commitment to supporting the ecosystem's continued development. Before I hand the call over to Joseph, I also want to briefly address the recent sale of Sharplink shares by Consensys Software Inc. While Consensys/MetaMask sold approximately 5.7 million common shares in October to better support its operating business, I want to emphasize that I did not sell any of my personal holdings. I have not sold any shares and continue to own over 5 million Sharplink shares personally, and Consensys and its affiliates retain significant additional equity interests in the company.

As one of Sharplink's largest shareholders and its Chairman, my conviction in our strategy and in the long-term Ethereum opportunity is as strong as ever. I'm fully committed to supporting Sharplink's continued growth and believe we are exceptionally well positioned to create meaningful long-term value for our shareholders. With that, I'd like to turn the call over to our Chief Executive Officer, Joseph Chalom, to discuss how Sharplink is translating this opportunity into disciplined execution and long-term shareholder value. Joseph?

Joseph Chalom: Thank you, Joe. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us. The third quarter represented an important turning point for the Ethereum ecosystem and Sharplink, highlighted by a meaningful recovery in the price of ETH, strong financial performance and continued execution of our long-term strategy. ETH appreciated approximately 72% during the third quarter, increasing from approximately $1,563 at the end of June to $2,681 as of September 30, 2026. Sharplink delivered double-digit revenue growth and materially higher net income compared to Q3 2025, benefiting from the appreciation of ETH and continued execution of our treasury strategy. The combination of growing staking revenue and a disciplined operating cost structure reinforces the operating leverage inherent in our treasury platform.

Beyond the financial results, Sharplink has made meaningful progress advancing several strategic initiatives designed to strengthen Ethereum's ecosystem, generate additional ETH and create long-term value for our shareholders. During the quarter, Sharplink continued to expand its leadership role within the Ethereum ecosystem, supporting initiatives designed to accelerate institutional adoption and strengthen the infrastructure underpinning Ethereum's next phase of growth. In addition to our previously announced support for EthLabs, Ethereum Institutional and EthSystems, we made a strategic equity investment in Blockspace, an Ethereum infrastructure company focused on validation and staking infrastructure. This investment further reinforces our commitment to supporting innovation and long-term growth across the Ethereum ecosystem.

Collectively, these organizations help establish the technological, institutional and operational foundations necessary for Ethereum to support a substantially larger share of global financial activity. Sharplink's involvement extends beyond providing financial support. It leverages our relationships, institutional expertise and broader ecosystem connectivity to support their development. Given our scale and position, Sharplink has an important opportunity to serve as a bridge between traditional finance and the Ethereum ecosystem, helping advance adoption while remaining focused on creating long-term value for our stockholders. Ultimately, our objective is to position Sharplink to benefit from Ethereum's expanding economic activity while identifying opportunities to grow ETH per share.

A central component of Sharplink's strategy is utilizing our ETH holdings as productive operating assets rather than simply maintaining passive exposure to Ethereum. A key advantage is our access to permanent capital, which enables us to pursue longer-term structured ETH deployments that may fit other investor mandates. Unlike capital that requires frequent withdrawals or rapid turnover, we can commit our ETH for multiyear periods, providing emerging on-chain protocols with the patient liquidity needed to establish and scale their operations. In return, we can negotiate differentiated economics designed to generate incremental ETH for our stockholders while supporting the development of the broader ecosystem.

We're focused on identifying these differentiated opportunities to deploy our treasury, generate additional ETH and enhance long-term stockholder value. During the quarter, we made meaningful progress activating several previously announced initiatives. In August, Sharplink announced a $200 million ETH allocation staked through Lido, further expanding our liquid staking capabilities. This deployment enables us to earn ETH staking rewards while maintaining flexibility to utilize tokenized staking positions across Ethereum's broader financial ecosystem. The allocation further diversifies our staking infrastructure and enhances our ability to evaluate additional on-chain opportunities, including using a portion of our Lido wrapped staked ETH as collateral to capitalize our Galaxy Sharplink On-Chain Yield Fund commitment.

In August, the Galaxy Sharplink On-Chain Yield Fund launched with $125 million of initial commitments, including $100 million from Sharplink and $25 million from Galaxy Digital. In Q3, the fund began deploying capital into on-chain investment opportunities, representing an important milestone in activating this strategy. We are in the beginning of a new phase we call On-Chain Finance 2.0. As more assets become tokenized, we expect RWA protocols to emerge to provide liquidity for trading and lending these assets. Additionally, new protocols continue to emerge as improved on-chain liquidity venues. However, these protocols will often have a cold start problem and need quality initial liquidity to ensure users have a good experience, enabling asset growth on their platforms.

By offering what we think of as jump-start capital out of the Galaxy Sharplink Fund, we can help solve this problem as more stablecoins and tokenized assets move on chain. This is part of how we want to put our ETH to work. Turning to broader capital allocation. Growing ETH per share continues to be our North Star, and we evaluate opportunities based on their ability to enhance stockholder value. As we disclosed on our last earnings call in June, Sharplink completed a $75 million registered direct financing at a premium to NAV with attached warrants, providing additional capital to acquire ETH and repurchase shares.

During the third quarter, Sharplink did not issue shares through its ATM program, reflecting our disciplined approach to raising capital and commitment to avoiding transactions that would dilute ETH exposure per share. We remain focused on maintaining flexibility across capital markets activities, including opportunistic financing, share repurchases and additional ETH acquisitions when market conditions support stockholder accretion. Our capital allocation decisions will continue to be guided by the economics of each opportunity and their potential to drive long-term value per share. Looking ahead, Sharplink is evaluating strategic opportunities across the digital asset ecosystem that could further expand our capabilities and take advantage of both our operating platform and permanent capital.

These could include operating businesses that address important industry needs, create additional sources of revenue or enable us to deploy our balance sheet better. We intend to remain selective, prioritizing opportunities that complement our ETH treasury strategy, meet our disciplined financial criteria and offer compelling potential for long-term stockholder value creation. The third quarter also brought meaningful developments across the global regulatory landscape, further supporting the institutional adoption of digital assets. While comprehensive market structure legislation in the United States remains unfinished following the Senate's failure to advance the CLARITY Act, we believe it's highly unlikely to be reintroduced given the results of last week's election.

That said, the SEC has advanced critical initiatives addressing tokenized securities, digital asset custody and pathways for broader institutional participation. Most notably, it has published an innovation exemption allowing for tokenization of U.S.-listed stocks and their trading on chain through SEC supervised venues built on public blockchains such as Ethereum. The SEC also proposed updating its transfer agency rules so that a blockchain can serve as a company's official record of stockholders. U.S. federal regulators continue its work in implementing the GENIUS Act stablecoin regulatory framework. On October 21, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issued its final rule for the stablecoin issuers it oversees.

The rule sets clear standards for the reserves behind each stablecoin, how holders can redeem them and how issuers manage risk. The GENIUS Act and the OCC's rule both take effect on January 18, 2027, when payment stablecoins in the U.S. come under federal framework for the first time. That gives banks, payment companies and asset managers the clarity they need to issue and use stablecoins at scale. The CFTC has also continued efforts to provide greater clarity around oversight and the operation of digital asset markets. The CFTC has continued to open U.S. derivative markets to digital assets and tokenization.

On November 3, it cleared perpetual futures on individual stocks to trade for the first time on exchanges registered with both the CFTC and the SEC. That builds on its approval of the first crypto perpetual futures contract in May. The CFTC has also made it easier to use digital assets as collateral. We believe these U.S. developments are increasingly important for banks, asset managers and other financial institutions evaluating how to incorporate blockchain technology into their operations. Greater regulatory clarity can reduce uncertainty and help institutions move from exploring digital assets to implementing practical on-chain financial applications. Although there is additional work to complete, the direction of regulatory progress is encouraging.

Sharplink's strategy does not depend on any single legislative or regulatory outcome. We continue to operate within existing regulatory frameworks while positioning our business to benefit from the continued institutional adoption of Ethereum. Moving beyond the U.S. regulatory landscape, I recently participated in Korea Blockchain Week in South Korea and TOKEN2049 in Singapore, which reinforced the growing momentum behind institutional adoption of Ethereum and digital assets globally. Having visited Asia 5 times over the last year, I've witnessed a notable shift in the conversation from retail trading towards institutional adoption and real-world financial applications. Throughout my travels in Asia, there was a clear impetus to not fall behind the U.S. from a digital asset innovation perspective.

In each country I visited, the priority is establishing the necessary regulatory foundations, including for local denominated stablecoins, tokenized assets and trusted interoperable infrastructure and clear rules for market participants. I had the opportunity to engage with sophisticated financial institutions, regulators and policymakers, and it was encouraging to see the growing interest in Ethereum and its Layer 2 ecosystem as foundational infrastructure for this next phase of financial innovation. These observations reinforce our conviction that Ethereum's credibly neutral infrastructure is well positioned to support the next generation of global finance, further strengthening Sharplink's long-term investment thesis and commitment to advancing the ecosystem. We continue to believe Ethereum is uniquely positioned to benefit from the convergence of 4 transformative trends.

First, stablecoins are bringing programmable money on chain. Second, tokenization is enabling traditional financial assets to operate on blockchain infrastructure. Third, on-chain finance is creating new opportunities for assets to be traded, financed and utilized in continuously operating markets. And fourth, AI agents bring automation and continuous attention on behalf of individuals and institutions. We believe agentic finance represents one of the most compelling opportunities emerging at the intersection of artificial intelligence, blockchain technology and global financial services. We've seen meaningful progress in the adoption of AI agents and the development of the infrastructure needed to support autonomous financial activity.

AI agents are moving beyond simple information retrieval and becoming part of our everyday lives, helping consumers manage schedules, book travel, compare products and make purchases. On-chain activity is also beginning to demonstrate the potential scale of this emerging agentic economy. As an example, hundreds of millions of agent-to-agent transactions have been recorded through the x402 micropayment protocol, which enables AI agents to pay for services, such as data, computing power and access to AI models. These developments provide early evidence of a shift towards autonomous systems capable of executing transactions and managing financial activities on behalf of both individuals and institutions.

As financial activity becomes increasingly automated, these AI agents will require access to programmable money, tokenized assets, deep liquidity and interoperable financial applications. We believe Ethereum is particularly well positioned to support this infrastructure given its established ecosystem and ability to facilitate financial activity across competing institutions and applications. Building on this thesis, in September, Sharplink published research exploring the potential scale of agentic finance, including a long-term scenario in which approximately $4 trillion in annual financial services revenue could be reshaped by 2035. While the timing and scale of adoption remains uncertain, the research underscores the potentially significant economic opportunity emerging at the intersection of AI, blockchain technology and global finance.

These developments are laying the foundation of what could become a multiyear institutional adoption cycle for Ethereum. Ethereum's established liquidity, developer ecosystem, security and credibly neutral infrastructure position it as compelling infrastructure for a more open and interconnected financial system. Its ability to support interoperable applications and programmable financial transactions offers meaningful advantages as traditional finance increasingly moves on chain. Overall, Q3 represented a strong quarter for Sharplink, driven by Ether's price appreciation, growth in our staking revenue and continued execution of our strategic priorities. We expanded our ETH yield strategies, deepened our engagement across the Ethereum ecosystem and strengthened our position to capitalize on emerging opportunities in institutional on-chain finance.

Looking ahead, we're focused on 3 priorities: growing ETH exposure per share through disciplined stockholder accretive capital allocation, deploying our treasury into differentiated opportunities designed to generate additional ETH and enhance the value of our holdings and leveraging our institutional expertise, relationships and strategic positioning to participate in Ethereum's continued evolution as foundational global financial infrastructure. Our conviction in Ethereum's long-term potential is as strong as ever. As institutional adoption accelerates and an increasing share of global financial activity moves on chain, we believe Sharplink is uniquely positioned to capitalize on this transformation. By leveraging our institutional-grade treasury platform, strategic relationships and disciplined capital allocation, we can compound ETH per share and create sustainable long-term value for our stockholders.

Before I hand it over to Bob to take us through our Q3 financial results, I'd like to directly address the recent crypto exchange hacks. Sharplink has had no direct or indirect exposure to these incidents. Sharplink's crypto assets are stored with U.S.-based qualified custodians in hardware isolated systems, the same principle as cold storage. Incidents like these underscore the importance of continuously strengthening industry safeguards, reinforcing institutional-grade practices and building the trust necessary to support broader institutional adoption and on-chain finance. With that, I'll turn the call over to Bob for a more detailed review of our third quarter financial results.

Robert DeLucia: Thank you, Joseph. I'll begin by encouraging everyone to review our quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2026, which we filed on Friday, November 6, 2026, with the SEC. The 10-Q provides detailed disclosures and footnotes that complement today's discussion, offering stockholders, analysts and investors a comprehensive view of Sharplink's financial position, liquidity and its treasury performance. We will now go through the financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. I'd like to remind everyone that all comparisons and variance commentary refer to the prior year quarter, unless otherwise specified. As of September 30, 2026, Sharplink held 602,361 native ETH with a net fair value of $1.6 billion.

In addition, we held 121,163 LsETH or liquid staked ETH, 66,379 weETH or wrapped ether.fi ETH and 57,393 of wstETH or Lido wrapped staked ETH with a combined net historical cost value of $482 million. Subsequent to quarter end, our combined ETH holdings have increased to 603,953 native ETH, 135,868 as-if redeemed LsETH, 73,601 as-if redeemed weETH and 81,695 as-if redeemed wstETH for a total of 895,117 ETH as of Monday, November 2, 2026. Total revenue for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was $13.5 million compared with $10.8 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase was driven by our staking and ETH yield generating strategies with staking revenue up 27% to $13.1 million.

We recorded a net realized gain of $75.2 million compared with a $6.3 million realized gain in the prior year quarter. The gain in the current quarter was primarily due to $55.6 million from LsETH redemptions, $18 million ETH staked for wstETH and $1.7 million from our contribution of wstETH to the Galaxy Sharplink On-Chain Yield Fund. We also recorded an unrealized gain of $676.7 million compared with a $107.3 million unrealized gain in Q3 of 2025. We also recorded an impairment charge of $1 million compared with a $7 million impairment charge in the prior year quarter. SG&A expenses in the third quarter were $11 million compared with $12 million in the prior year quarter.

The decrease reflects the elimination of $3.1 million in quarterly asset manager fees following the termination of our asset management agreements in May 2026. These decreases were partially offset by increases of $1 million in salary and benefits and $1.2 million in stock-based compensation, both primarily attributable to additional personnel hired after the third quarter of 2025 as we were building out our ETH treasury operating team. For the third quarter of 2026, we reported net income of $751.4 million compared to net income of $104.3 million in the prior year quarter.

The Q3 2026 results were primarily driven by the previously discussed unrealized fair value gain of $676.7 million and the $75.2 million of realized gains, which were offset by an impairment charge of $1 million. Overall, our third quarter performance reflects the recovery in ETH prices during the quarter from approximately $1,563 per ETH at June 30, 2026 to approximately $2,681 at September 30, 2026. As we've noted previously, the impairment charges and unrealized gains recorded this quarter reflect the current market pricing dynamics and are accounted for under U.S. GAAP. Just as in prior periods, impairment charges do not represent realized economic losses, and this quarter's unrealized gains do not represent actual realized economic gains.

Neither of these amounts change the number of ETH units we hold. Our treasury strategy continues to be evaluated on the disciplined ETH accumulation and the long-term productivities of those assets over time. As of September 30, 2026, cash on hand was $47.9 million compared to cash on hand of $28.5 million as of December 31, 2025. Between our cash position, our unencumbered ETH holdings and the flexibility of our capital allocation framework, we believe Sharplink maintains ample liquidity going forward to execute on its strategy across a range of market conditions and opportunities.

For additional details, our complete financial statements with accompanying footnotes, including all required disclosures and management's MD&A analysis are contained in the quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2026, filed with the SEC. This concludes our prepared remarks. We will now open it up for questions from those participating on the call. Operator, back to you.

Devin Ryan: Okay. I appreciate it. Is there any way to think about for the Galaxy fund, what the expected return? I know it's strategic as well, but if there's a kind of a targeted return on that capital?

Joseph Chalom: Sure. If you take a step back, the fund is designed to generate steady returns above traditional ETH staking. I would think of those as singles and doubles. Joseph Chalom: Thank you, Fedor. Blockspace, in particular, is focused on a few critical areas of Ethereum's infrastructure. It includes block building, validation and staking. Each of these are fundamental to the network's security, efficiency and continued development. We view our Blockspace equity investment as a strategic investment that complements our core ETH treasury strategy.

Again, our North Star and priority is growing ETH per share, and we're going to do that through disciplined capital allocation and treasury management.

So you can think of it less as a vertical integration play, but helping support really important infrastructure with potential economic upside as an equity investor.

Fedor Shabalin: And if you allow the follow-up, it's my follow-up, kind of follow up on Devin's question on Ethereum adoption overall. You know that accelerating institutional adoption positions Sharplink to grow ETH per share. But maybe which adoption milestones near term do you see as most consequential for Ethereum price? Maybe if you can, maybe it's a good time to rehash the -- like this theoretical equation, which variables should move and how much Ethereum in theory should respond, just like a pure quantification question, if it makes sense.

Joseph Chalom: It does. So I think in the short term, you should think of the 2 most important being the growth of stablecoin circulation and the growth of tokenized assets. Both of those primitives are dominated on the Ethereum ecosystem. Over 50% of all stablecoin circulation and transaction is on Ethereum. The same is true on tokenization. I personally believe tokenization is where most of the highest value activity is going to start from, and then it's going to happen on chain. And so DeFi and On-Chain activity was built on Ethereum. It has the predominance of that activity.

And as you start combining stablecoins as the money layer, tokenization as the asset exposure layer and third, on-chain execution, I think you'll end up seeing a lot more activity by more and more institutional users. In the longer run, I believe agentic finance will help automate and continuously execute these transactions. But I think in the immediate term, it's mostly going to be stablecoins, tokenized assets on DeFi and on-chain activity. For most of its history, Ethereum has been building and doing the hard work, which is ensuring it has the security, the neutrality, the censorship resistance, that distinguishes it from every other blockchain around.

I think you're now going to see the phase of more and more transaction activity. The newest releases coming from Ethereum will significantly reduce costs and increase speeds, and that will inure to the Ethereum price. I also think Ethereum is a store of value, and it's starting to get more and more attention in that regard. So I think the short term, stablecoins, tokenization and on-chain activity in the longer term, it's going to be agentic transactions.

Kevin Dede: I just cursory analysis here, but it looked like native staking fees increased sequentially. And I was wondering if you might address that.

Joseph Chalom: So the native Ethereum staking is driven by supply-demand dynamics and the actual yield is dynamic in nature. We've seen periods where it was around 3%. We've also seen periods recently where it was around 2.5%. Right now, if you look back over the last quarter, it's been averaging a little bit closer to 2.65%, but that will change over time. We're less concerned with the actual yield. We're more concerned and focused on making sure that we're deploying our entire balance sheet, and we're doing it in a way that's safe and disciplined. But it is based on supply and demand dynamics. We saw a period over the last 1.5 years since ETF started staking and more importantly, the digital asset treasury started staking where the percentage of staking rates on Ethereum is now north of 35%, and that will drive both the yield you receive as well as the queue and unqueue time for staking your ETH.

Kevin Dede: I apologize, Joseph, I think I misframed my question. I was more curious about the validator fees, in fact, that Sharplink is paying. It looked like they were up almost 100 basis points sequentially. And I was wondering how you think we should think about that. I understand the fluidity in ETH staking returns. Just not sure about in light of Fedor's question, too, right, with your Blockspace investments, how you plan on managing native staking?

Joseph Chalom: Sure. Most of our native staking is done on a delegated basis, Kevin, through both Coinbase and Anchorage. And we pay them a fixed percentage of our staking rewards, single digit, low single digits. I can't go into the details for confidentiality. But the amount of absolute fees we share on both custody and staking rewards will depend on the total AUM that's being staked. But that's managed primarily through our relationships with Anchorage Digital and Coinbase.

It's a fixed percentage of our ETH rewards being received, but we'll receive more rewards as the price of ETH expands.

Kevin Dede: KPMG as your auditors, how much oversight will they actually have over the Galaxy fund and the Linea DeFi activity? Just kind of curious about how auditors are going to resolve the intricacies of decentralized finance.

Joseph Chalom: Sure. I mean, the auditors are involved in auditing and classifying the income and revenue from every deployment we make, whether it's the Linea, ether.fi, Eigen, Lido deployments, they're actively involved. They are independent auditors, and they focus on GAAP standards and issue opinions and audit our financials. With respect to the Galaxy fund, the fund has its own auditors. Galaxy as the manager of the fund publishes accounting and NAV reports. But then how it's classified is -- how the returns are classified is handled by KPMG as our external auditor. I don't think there's anything more to share. We work very closely with them, and we rely on them to help audit our financials.

Operator: Our next question is from Brian Kinstlinger with Alliance Global Partners.

Kevin Pimental: This is Kevin on for Brian. Are you having discussions with Galaxy or others about other funds where you can deploy capital?

Joseph Chalom: Just taking a step back, when we started our strategy in June of 2025, we didn't have in-house capabilities to do full asset management. So we had engaged initially on a nonexclusive basis, 2 asset managers to help us on our ETH purchases and staking. As we disclosed in May, for the basic asset management capabilities, we've terminated those external relationships. We have really positive relationships with both those managers, but we've built in-house teams capable of doing these deployments, as you've seen, including the ether.fi and Lido deployments. But when we try to do on-chain deployments in scale, we engaged Galaxy in this fund together, where together, we've allocated 100 -- sorry, we've committed $125 million of assets.

Galaxy has unique capabilities to not only source these opportunities, but to deploy and monitor them in scale. That's why in this high value-add engagement, we did it through a fund structure. Kevin, I would tell you, on a weekly basis, we're meeting with protocols, DeFi providers, fund managers to explore opportunities, but we haven't announced anything new. So right now, many of the initial deployments are done in-house. We do our staking oversight in-house, but we have this one fund structure with Galaxy to do on-chain yield and to do it in scale.

Kevin Pimental: Great. And then just a second one. How important do you view Glamsterdam to Ethereum's investment thesis? And are you seeing any developments from the upgrade that could materially improve Ethereum's economics or the institutional adoption?

Joseph Chalom: Joe Lubin, I'll turn this one over to you.

Joseph Lubin: Sure. Thank you. So Glamsterdam is certainly important to the evolution of the Ethereum platform. In terms of institutional adoption, I think it's relatively immaterial. It certainly does provide some benefits in reducing our reliance on centralization in the proposer-builder separation construct. It will increase throughput. It is adjusting pricing. But the institutions are coming anyway. And I think from what we're seeing, institutional adoption is effectively independent of the advancements of Glamsterdam.

Operator: Our next question is from Joseph Vafi with Canaccord Genuity.

Joseph Vafi: Nice progress on a bunch of fronts. I was just wondering at a high level, if we think about GENIUS Act being fully implemented here early in the year, along with some of the RWA, how do you see it kind of maybe at a high level, how that may ultimately move spot, how there may be a bit of a decoupling effect from other correlated assets and how those trends help the underlying native staking yield? And then I have a quick follow-up.

Joseph Chalom: Sure. When I think about the CLARITY Act, which didn't pass cloture in the Senate, we were actually quite happy with what the SEC and CFTC have done since. The 2 most important green lights we have for institutions are GENIUS. And I had mentioned in my opening remarks, the OCC guidance around stablecoins and the fact that the GENIUS Act will take effect in January of 2027. That will unlock the world's largest institutions to start participating in stablecoins. The second is the SEC's innovation exemption, which is providing a 5-year ramp and clarity to tokenization to allow certain venues that are not necessarily national stock exchanges to do automated market making and support U.S. equity tokenization.

We're going to start seeing that on NASDAQ, New York Stock Exchange, but we're also seeing important developments on the DTCC front, the ability to dematerialize collateral in accounts and allow them to be tokenized so that members can move them from one account to another in a very, very rapid intraday manner. What both of these things are going to do is stimulate stablecoin circulation and use cases as well as tokenization of U.S. equities. And when those 2 things happen, we believe the activity over 50% historically will happen in the Ethereum ecosystem. We'll see more users come online. We'll see institutions go from experimentation to production.

And then the interesting element is when you have these tokenized assets for the first time, we have an ability to see them borrowed against, lent against on chain, whether you call it DeFi or on-chain 2.0, that's where you're going to see a lot of the composability. And we see Ethereum being at the forefront of that activity, and it's going to benefit the price of Ether. I won't make short-term price predictions, but this is the exact thesis we've been talking about since last June, and we're seeing it play out live in real time.

And we're quite encouraged by the fact that the SEC, CFTC and OCC are providing the guidance needed for the world's largest institutions to come on chain. While it's starting in the U.S., we're very encouraged by what we're seeing in Asia as well.

Joseph Vafi: Great color, Joseph. And then quickly on the registered direct during the quarter. Obviously, you have a lot of liquidity with your balance, and I understand it was accretive to ETH per share. Just -- maybe just a few extra thoughts on kind of the strategic use here of the registered direct in the quarter.

Joseph Chalom: Sure. I think we've said publicly that when our multiple to NAV is below 1, we are not in the business of raising capital through the ATM because it could be dilutive for shareholders. We used the ATM last year when it was accretive to shareholders. But the interesting thing about running an Ethereum treasury company is we have every day the flexibility across multiple investment opportunities. Obviously, we own ETH directly, and that gives our clients and our investors an opportunity to get the capital appreciation. But when we think of disciplined capital allocation, we are opportunistic. There are moments where it doesn't make sense to raise. I would tell you it's very sentiment oriented.

When the price of ETH in Q3 expanded, the number of calls coming in from institutions, whether they were hedge funds or banks, interested in buying our shares through registered directs increased, but we're going to be very, very careful. And where it makes sense, we've done it twice. We will do the premium to NAV financing. At the same time, you've seen our cash on hand has expanded. It's just shy of $50 million, which gives us every day an opportunity to make a decision around share repurchases or ETH acquisitions. You would have seen in June when we raised the $75 million, we did both. We raised capital accretively.

We did some share repurchases, and we also bought ETH. So we have a team who's able to do that. We're not in a rush, and we're not here to accumulate ETH for the sake of accumulation. We're going to do things that make sense for our long-term investment thesis and grow ETH per share. That is how we think about it. It doesn't change in an upmarket or a down market. We have the flexibility, and that's the beauty of an Ethereum treasury strategy.

We are seeing a lot of inbounds, but we're going to be very careful and thoughtful to do financing when it makes sense, to do stock repurchases when it makes sense and to buy ETH when it's accretive for investors.

Operator: We have reached the end of the question-and-answer session. I would like to turn the floor back over to Joseph Chalom for closing comments.

Joseph Chalom: Thank you, operator, and thank you to everyone who's joined us today. I believe Sharplink is entering an exciting new phase of its evolution and strategy. We've established a strong institutional foundation. We've assembled an experienced team and built one of the world's largest ETH treasuries. And we're leveraging that scale every day to pursue new opportunities to deepen our strategic relationships and to generate additional ETH through disciplined capital allocation and innovative on-chain deployments. And while market conditions continue to evolve day by day, we are relentlessly focused on compounding our ETH per share and creating sustainable long-term value for our stockholders.

Thank you again for your continued support, and we look forward to updating you again on our next earnings call. Have a great day, everyone.

Operator: This concludes today's teleconference. You may disconnect your lines at this time. Thank you for your participation.

#3113. Anthropic Introduces New Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 AI Models

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Overkill for the average user, but the models are smarter than ever for professionals.

Anthropic took the wraps off yet another set of AI models on Monday, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, which are ready to use and make substantial improvements over their predecessors. While an average user may not see the benefits of the latest models, Anthropic says they’re best for the “most ambitious, open-ended work.”

The new Claude models show greatly improved metrics in areas like coding (don’t they all?), reasoning, vision, cybersecurity and biology. The latter of which have strong safeguards against misuse in the Fable model, which give Anthropic enough confidence to release it to the public.

Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 generate output up to 30% faster than their predecessors and are available at lower prices — a trend we’ve continued to see lately with most new AI model releases.

Anthropic dropped a series of benchmarks showing off how much better the new models are compared with the previous ones. And generally, they’re impressive. Fable 5.2 outperforms Fable 5.1 in one agentic coding benchmark at 49.1% versus 32.4% at “Xhigh effort,” bringing a meaningful distance in performance. As far as cybersecurity benchmarks are concerned, Mythos 5.2 scores a jump from 61.7% to 76.3% — a rather impressive jump — if you’re using the model to its fullest potential.

Anthropic says Claude Mythos 5.2 is its most capable model for cybersecurity engineering. The new model is capable of catching more vulnerabilities and is better at reproducing and fixing them. That said, Mythos 5.2’s cybersecurity features are locked to a specific group right now: Anthropic’s Cyber Verification Program.

The company boasted about enhanced capabilities in the latest model improvements in mathematics, science and engineering. It also says that testers of Fable 5.2 found the new model more capable of more ambiguous tasks that require abstract reasoning when it came to research and analysis.

Anthropic makes a big deal about the alignment of Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. Alignment tracks whether and how the intention of the (human) user is executed by the model. And as agentic AI becomes more prevalent, there are more stories of AI deciding to go out of its way to complete a task, even with devastating consequences. Fable 5.2 includes guardrails that block risky cybersecurity activities — like penetration testing and exploit generation — and advanced biology capabilities.
